title: SYMMETRY-REDUCED strict h=0 K=4 (4 identical agents) CRRA REE contour-Phi fixed-point study

task1_cython_port.operator_used_for_study: Numba phi_K4_halo (parallel=True, 4 threads) -- faster than the single-threaded Cython port; symmetry reduction is the main tractability win, so we use the faster operator. Cython port built + bit-exact validated.

validation.note: Cython kernel reproduces the Numba operator BIT-EXACTLY (0.0 diff) over the full 13^4 grid on the NL IC and a random P. Built with -O3, fastmath OFF (matches Numba fastmath=False).

speed.note: Cython is single-threaded; Numba uses prange over 4 cores. Cython matches exactly but is ~3.4x slower here, so the study uses the parallel Numba operator.

task2_symmetry.representation: sorted index tuples (multisets) i1<=i2<=i3<=i4 over the inner grid
task2_symmetry.note: Phi maps symmetric->symmetric BIT-EXACTLY (asymmetry of Phi(symmetric P) = 0.0, far below the 1e-12 target). The reduced phi_red = reduce(phi_full(expand(v))) is therefore exact; orbit-average vs representative-read agree to 4e-16.

picard_oscillation.verdict: K=4 does NOT show the K=3 period-2 learning oscillation. Undamped Picard from the NL IC drives the revelation deficit to ~0.0003 (essentially fully revealing) within ~5 iters, while ||F||inf falls from 0.43 to a small NON-SMOOTH plateau ~0.012-0.020 (mean 0.0165) where it wobbles irregularly (NOT a clean 2-cycle: |P_t - P_(t-2)| ~0.04-0.05 stays comparable to ||F||inf). So a non-smooth residual floor recurs, but at ~0.015 (vs K=3's ~0.2) and the limit is FR, not a partially-revealing 2-cycle.
